title: Friends
hook: a friend loves at all times (Proverbs 17:17)
tomorrow: is your neighbor everyone on earth, or the person next door?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a son on the cross making sure his mother had a home: honor grows. Today, the people nobody assigns us. We pick them.

Two sayings from the same book, a few pages apart. One: “A friend loveth at all times.” The other: “Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” Wounds, faithful? Kisses, deceitful? Some friendships run on the opposite rule: hype each other up, never say the hard thing. So which is it in Proverbs: the friend who always loves, or the friend who wounds?
screen: `A FRIEND LOVETH AT ALL TIMES.` → `FAITHFUL ARE THE WOUNDS.` → `WHICH IS IT?`

segments.voice: It's the same friend. Look at the whole first line: “A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.” At all times: the good days, the long ordinary middle, and the day something has to be said. A friend who only flatters loves at some times. The wound is faithful because it's honest, and because it comes from someone who's staying. Flattery costs nothing; honesty risks the friendship, and a friend takes that risk. Proverbs also notices that friendship takes work: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.” Then, at supper on his last night, Jesus takes the word for himself: “Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.” In John's telling, a friend is someone you let in and tell the truth to. Here's one to repeat tonight: the same book that praises a friend's love praises a friend's wounds, and sees no contradiction. So at all times includes two hard things: hearing the honest word, and saying the true, kind one back.
screen: `IT'S THE SAME FRIEND.` · `A WOUND THAT STAYS.` · `SHEW HIMSELF FRIENDLY.` · `I HAVE CALLED YOU FRIENDS.` · then, large: `AT ALL TIMES.`

segments.voice: Bring one friend to mind: someone who has been there at all times, or once told you a hard truth you needed. Say their name quietly, and one thing they mean to you, as if they could hear it. If you pray, thank God for them by name.
Friends. People who love at all times: the good days, the ordinary ones, and the day something hard has to be said.
The line to keep: at all times, the honest words and the staying included. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Christians often see friendship as part of faith, since Jesus calls his disciples friends; some pray for friends by name, and some churches value spiritual friendship, where friends help each other grow.

tell her honestly, and kindly, what you think.

chat.says: nia finally said it: 'you always leave early for church stuff.' it stung. is she even being a friend?
options: Yes. Faithful are the wounds of a friend. She told you the hard thing because she's staying.
No. A friend loveth at all times, so a real friend never says anything that hurts.
Doesn't matter. Faith comes first, so a friend who complains about church can go.
chat.meaning: Proverbs holds both: a friend loveth at all times, and faithful are the wounds of a friend. Loving at all times includes the honest, hard word.
